---
title: "The prior"
subtitle: "Scientist session 1"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: false
---

The decision this prior is allowed to support is a productivity benchmark. It does not set a catch limit.

A Schaefer model gives $F_{MSY} = r/2$. The FishLife mean is already off that value, because steepness and natural mortality have moved the shape. The CV is not in `data/lhs.RData`. The value in the marked block is the one you set. A species row starts at 0.2. A genus row is wider.

The assessment $F_{MSY}$ for blue shark is about 0.18. That number is not in the marked block, and this file will not print it. The prior is the FishLife mean.

## Change this block

```{r inputs}
# species: one row of data/lhs.RData
# genus:   mean of every species in that genus; raise cv
# stock:   ignore the table and use r_stock and fmsy_stock

genus      <- "Prionace"
species    <- "glauca"
level      <- "species"
cv         <- 0.2

r_stock    <- 0.04
fmsy_stock <- 0.03
```

```{r prior, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
candidates <- c(file.path("data", "lhs.RData"), file.path("..", "data", "lhs.RData"))
lhs_path <- candidates[file.exists(candidates)][1]
if (is.na(lhs_path)) stop("data/lhs.RData was not found.")
load(lhs_path)

if (level == "stock") {
  r <- r_stock
  fmsy <- fmsy_stock
  used <- "values typed above"
} else if (level == "species") {
  row <- lhs[lhs$Genus == genus & lhs$Species == species, ]
  if (nrow(row) != 1) stop("That species is not in the table. Set level to stock and type the values.")
  r <- row$r
  fmsy <- exp(row$fmsy)
  used <- paste(genus, species)
} else if (level == "genus") {
  rows <- lhs[lhs$Genus == genus, ]
  if (nrow(rows) < 1) stop("That genus is not in the table.")
  r <- mean(rows$r)
  fmsy <- exp(mean(rows$fmsy))
  used <- paste0(genus, " (", nrow(rows), " species)")
} else {
  stop("level must be species, genus, or stock.")
}

schaefer <- r / 2
sigma <- sqrt(log(1 + cv^2))
f_lo <- fmsy * exp(-1.96 * sigma)
f_hi <- fmsy * exp(1.96 * sigma)

result <- data.frame(
  Item = c("Level", "Used", "r", "FishLife Fmsy", "Schaefer r/2", "CV", "Fmsy low", "Fmsy high", "Productivity score"),
  Value = c(
    level,
    used,
    sprintf("%.3f", r),
    sprintf("%.3f", fmsy),
    sprintf("%.3f", schaefer),
    sprintf("%.2f", cv),
    sprintf("%.3f", f_lo),
    sprintf("%.3f", f_hi),
    "copy from the 2018 risk assessment"
  )
)
```

```{r show, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(result, col.names = c("Item", "Value"))
```

The interval is a lognormal 95% range around the FishLife median, using the CV in the marked block. It is the width you set, not a covariance from FishLife.

```{r figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=3}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(data.frame(fmsy = fmsy, f_lo = f_lo, f_hi = f_hi), ggplot2::aes(y = 1)) +
    ggplot2::geom_errorbar(ggplot2::aes(xmin = f_lo, xmax = f_hi), width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.8, orientation = "y") +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(x = fmsy), size = 3) +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = schaefer, linetype = 2) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      x = "FMSY",
      y = NULL,
      title = "FishLife median and the interval from the CV you set",
      subtitle = "Dashed line: Schaefer FMSY = r/2"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 13)
} else {
  plot(1, 1, type = "n", xlim = range(f_lo, f_hi, schaefer), ylim = c(0, 1), ylab = "", yaxt = "n", xlab = "FMSY")
  segments(f_lo, 0.5, f_hi, 0.5)
  points(fmsy, 0.5, pch = 16)
  abline(v = schaefer, lty = 2)
}
```

*Prionace* has one species in the table, so genus and species print the same mean. *Alopias* has two, so the genus mean moves. Someone without a case sets `genus` to `Isurus` and `species` to `oxyrinchus`.
